title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the surrounding pages: X -> S is a smooth family, essentially of curves, with S a complex manifold or smooth algebraic variety. The D_i are differential operators on S and the omega_i are relative 1-forms. Statement (3) is a Picard-Fuchs type relation, Sum_i D_i Int_{gamma_s} omega_i = 0 for all cycles gamma_s in the fibres. Criterion (7) says the same operator, lifted to X as D-bar_i by a local connection (a local splitting of X -> S), sends Sum omega_i to a relatively exact form: Sum D-bar_i omega_i = d_{X/S} phi, which defines phi in (10). The quantity mu(a,b) = Sum_i D_i Int_{a(s)}^{b(s)} omega_i is the 'inhomogeneous' Picard-Fuchs value on an abelian integral between two sections a and b. By (14), mu(a,b) = phi(b(s)) - phi(a(s)) when a and b are horizontal.

The page proves that (7) is sufficient for (3), first via chains with horizontal boundary. By additivity, one reduces to the case where a(s0) is close to b(s0). One can then work in a small open set of X on which a (flat) connection, i.e. a local product structure, exists, and 'on gagne'.

A second route treats cycles Z_s of any dimension. If the omega'_i are absolute forms lifting the relative ones, then Sum D_{i,s} Int_{Z_s} omega'_i = Int_{Z_s} (Sum D-bar_i omega'_i)_s. The right side vanishes because (Sum D-bar_i omega'_i)_s is relatively exact and exact forms integrate to zero on cycles. The key identity is boxed as (15): D_s Int_{Z_s} omega'_s = Int_{Z_s} (D-bar omega')_s. This is differentiation under the integral along a horizontally transported cycle: the Lie derivative along a lifted vector field computes the derivative of periods. In modern terms it says the algebraic Gauss-Manin connection on relative de Rham cohomology is dual to the flat (Gauss-Manin) connection on the local system of fibre homology. Grothendieck calls this the 'essential transcendental property' of the connection, admits it without proof, and next page uses it with de Rham's theorem on the fibres to justify Picard-Fuchs relations.

The programme on the next page is to compute mu(a,b) 'algebraically, without computing integrals'. This is exactly the mechanism of Manin's homomorphism in his proof of Mordell over function fields: a Picard-Fuchs operator applied to an abelian integral between sections gives an algebraic function.
errors: For (15) to hold, D-bar must be a lift of D compatible with d, e.g. built from Lie derivatives along lifted vector fields of a local connection, and omega' must restrict to closed forms on the fibres. Both hypotheses are implicit. Index notation is inconsistent (D_s vs D_{is}, omega_i vs omega'_i).
The additivity reduction to a(s0) near b(s0) tacitly uses the existence of horizontal sections through intermediate points, which needs local triviality; fine for smooth families.

ideas.what: Criterion for a Picard-Fuchs relation: the lifted operator applied to the relative forms gives a relatively exact form, so the operator kills all periods.
ideas.modern_name: Picard-Fuchs equations via Gauss-Manin connection / Griffiths-Dwork style reduction
ideas.where_published: Gauss-Manin is mentioned in Grothendieck's 1966 IHES de Rham cohomology paper; no explicit Picard-Fuchs criterion known to me

ideas.what: (15): derivative of a period equals the period of the Lie-derivative-type lift D-bar omega'.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility of algebraic Gauss-Manin connection with the flat connection on the homology local system (differentiation under the integral sign)

ideas.what: mu(a,b): Picard-Fuchs operator applied to an abelian integral between two sections, computed algebraically as phi(b) - phi(a) via horizontal sections.
ideas.modern_name: Manin homomorphism / Manin map (inhomogeneous Picard-Fuchs, normal functions)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful pedagogical exposition of the classical Gauss-Manin / Picard-Fuchs mechanism, including the Manin-map computation of mu(a,b). Everything here is classical and in the literature (Manin, Katz-Oda, Deligne, Coleman); the only mild interest is Grothendieck's own working-through of Manin's construction.
transcription_corrections: Lines 1-5 read roughly: '...point soit on est ramené au cas où a(s0) est proche de b(s0), il suffit qu'on puisse se placer dans un ouvert de X assez petit pour qu'il y ait une connexion. Et on gagne.'
'si la dimension est > un zéro [?]' should probably read 'où le deuxième membre est un zéro' (i.e. the second side vanishes), followed by 'car ∫_{Z_s} ω_s = 0 si ω est un bord'.
'est une forme définie produits [?] {+relative+}' likely reads 'est une forme relative qui est un bord' ('relative' written above a struck word).
The final lines read: 'qui donne la propriété transcendante essentielle de la connexion intégrable considérée ici. Nous n'allons pas prouver (15) ici, et l'admettrons, mais notons que'.
The integrands in the unnumbered formula carry primes (ω'_i) on the right-hand side, and the left-hand operator is D_{is}.
